session.prompt: A spam raid just hit #general. Preview the cleanup, then remove it.

calls.result: would_delete: the 4 most recent messages in #general, with their IDs
asks you to confirm 4 messages in #general; on yes, deleted: the 4 IDs, nothing else

recipes.title: Catch up on a channel and post a recap
recipes.goal: You were away. You want to know what happened in a busy channel, then share a short recap with the team.

steps.prompt: What happened in #support since yesterday morning? Group it by topic.
steps.does: Finds the channel by name, then reads its messages from that point on. Each call returns up to 100 messages, so the assistant pages forward on a busy channel.

steps.prompt: Which of these questions got no answer?
steps.does: Works from the messages it already read. If a thread holds the answer, it lists the channel's threads and reads them too.

steps.prompt: Post the recap in #team as an embed, then pin it.
steps.does: Sends one embed with a title and a field per topic, then pins the new message.

notes: Message bodies come back empty when Message Content is off in the Developer Portal. See [Troubleshooting](#empty-messages).

recipes.title: Stop a raid without guessing
recipes.goal: New accounts flood #general with the same link. You want the spam gone and the accounts out, and you want to see each mass action before it runs.

steps.prompt: Read the last 50 messages in #general. Which authors posted the same link?
steps.does: Reads the channel. Every message carries its `author_id`, so the assistant can group the spam by account without a member search.

steps.prompt: Time out those accounts for one hour while we look.
steps.does: Times out each member. A timeout is undone with a duration of 0, so this step is easy to take back.

steps.prompt: Delete those spam messages. Show me the preview first.
steps.does: Runs a dry run on the IDs of the spam it read and lists each message with its author and age, then waits. It deletes only when called again with `dry_run: false` and those IDs, so a message posted meanwhile stays. Messages older than 14 days are deleted one by one, more slowly.

steps.prompt: Ban the accounts that only posted spam. List them before you ban anyone.
steps.does: The dry run returns the user IDs it would send to Discord. After your go, the real call returns which bans succeeded and which failed.

steps.prompt: Show me the audit log for the last hour.
steps.does: Reads who did what: your bans and timeouts, and anything another moderator did meanwhile.

notes: The bot can only time out, kick or ban members whose highest role sits below its own. Discord refuses to time out the server owner or a member with Administrator.
Messages older than 14 days are deleted one by one: Discord allows about 40, then asks for a pause of about 2 minutes, and the tool says how long to wait.

recipes.title: Run a community event
recipes.goal: You host a monthly community call. You want the event created, announced with a link, and a headcount on the day.

steps.prompt: Create an event called Community call next Friday at 8 PM in the Town hall voice channel.
steps.does: Finds the voice channel, then creates the event. A voice or stage event needs its channel; an external event needs a location and an end time instead.

steps.prompt: Make an invite to the event and announce it in #announcements.
steps.does: Creates an invite that opens the event, then posts the announcement with the link.

steps.prompt: Publish the announcement to the servers that follow #announcements.
steps.does: Crossposts the message. This works only in an announcement channel, once per message.

steps.prompt: How many people are interested? Move the start to 8:30 PM.
steps.does: Lists the interested users, then changes only the start time of the event.

notes: Creating an event needs the Create Events permission. Manage Events alone no longer suffices.

For a voice event, the bot also needs View Channel and Connect in that channel. The invite link does not grant Connect: grant it on a role the bot holds or in the channel's overwrites. A stage event needs Manage Channels, Mute Members and Move Members instead, and the invite link grants only Manage Channels.

recipes.title: Restructure channels and roles in one pass
recipes.goal: Your server grew without a plan. You want new categories, a staff area, a Helper role and the right permissions, reviewed once and then applied together.

steps.prompt: Look at my channels, roles and permissions. Propose a layout with an Events category, a private Staff category and a Helper role. Do not change anything yet.
steps.does: Reads the current structure and replies with a plan: what it would create, move and allow, in order. Nothing changes on Discord in this step.

steps.prompt: Apply the plan.
steps.does: Creates the role and the categories, moves the channels, and puts the role where the plan says. For the private category it grants the bot View Channel before it denies @everyone, then syncs the channels inside with their category.

steps.prompt: Check that Helpers can see #help but not the Staff category.
steps.does: Reads the overwrites on the channels it changed and compares them with the plan.

steps.prompt: Delete the old #events-old channel.
steps.does: Runs a dry run first and names the channel it would delete. It deletes only when called again with `dry_run: false`.

notes: For the steps with no dry run, the preview is the plan in the first step, and your client's prompt before each write, if it asks.
Deny @everyone View Channel only after the bot has its own allow: otherwise the bot loses sight of the channel. Only Administrator ignores channel overwrites.
The bot can only edit, assign or move roles below its own highest role. New roles are placed below it.

recipes.title: Set up a support forum with tags
recipes.goal: Questions get lost in a chat channel. You want a forum where each question is a post, tagged by type, and closed when solved.

steps.prompt: Create a forum called help in the Support category.
steps.does: Finds the category, then creates the forum channel in it.

steps.prompt: Give it the tags Bug, Question, Feature request and Solved. Only moderators can apply Solved.
steps.does: Sets the forum's tags. A moderated tag can only be applied by members with Manage Threads.

steps.prompt: Open a first post that explains how to ask a good question.
steps.does: Creates the post with its title and starter message.

steps.prompt: List the posts tagged Bug. Mark the fixed ones Solved and archive them.
steps.does: Lists the forum's posts, reads the ones in question, then updates their tags and archives them. Archiving closes a post without deleting it.

notes: `discord_set_forum_tags` replaces the whole tag list. A tag you leave out is deleted from the forum, so ask the assistant to read the current tags first when you only add one.

recipes.title: Post notifications through a webhook
recipes.goal: Release notes and alerts should arrive in #releases under their own name and avatar, as tidy embeds.

steps.prompt: Create a webhook named Release notes in #releases.
steps.does: Creates the webhook and returns its ID and token.

steps.prompt: Post the notes for version 2.0 through it as an embed with a field per change.
steps.does: Sends the message through the webhook. The token authorizes the send, so the bot needs no permission in the channel for it.

steps.prompt: Fix the typo in the second field of that message.
steps.does: Edits the message it sent, through the same webhook.

notes: A webhook token lets anyone post through it, with or without this server. Keep it out of shared chats and repositories. Delete the webhook to revoke the token.
`discord_list_webhooks` returns tokens, even in read-only mode. Leave the webhooks toolset out when you do not need it.

recipes.title: Audit who can do what
recipes.goal: Before you open the server to more people, you want to know which channels are restricted, which roles hold strong permissions, and who changed them lately.

steps.prompt: Audit the permissions of my server. Which channels deny @everyone, and which roles have Administrator or Manage Server?
steps.does: Builds a report of every channel overwrite, with role and member names, and lists the roles with their permissions.

steps.prompt: Who holds the Moderator role? What can Alex do on the server?
steps.does: Lists the role's members, then one member's roles and server-wide permissions. Those come from roles only: channel overwrites are not applied.

steps.prompt: Who changed roles or channels this week?
steps.does: Reads the audit log, filtered by action type when you ask for one.

notes: Channels the bot cannot view are left out of the audit and counted in `hiddenChannels`. Grant the bot View Channel on them to include them.
